security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, TypeScript examples, and Convex ctx.db snippets. Confirmed risk is limited to documented Convex CLI validation commands that execute local project tooling. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious hidden behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running Convex CLI commands, and mention possible network, package, and deployment effects.
Add a note that API keys must stay server-side, avoid logs, and only pass to trusted component code.

content.value_statement: Convex components are easy to overbuild or wire incorrectly. This skill guides structure, boundaries, wrappers, and validation for reusable backend modules.
actual_capabilities: Chooses local, packaged, or hybrid component structure from the documented decision tree.
Defines component-owned tables and public Convex functions with validators.
Wires components into an app with app.use and app-side wrappers.
Keeps authentication, environment values, and HTTP routes at the app boundary.
Guides Convex codegen and dev validation for generated components.
limitations: It assumes the project already uses Convex.
It cannot configure Convex deployment credentials for the user.
It does not replace security review of generated backend logic.
Packaged components still need package build and example app validation.

use_cases.title: Extract App Logic
use_cases.description: Move reusable backend workflows into a local Convex component with isolated tables and app wrappers.

use_cases.title: Package Shared Modules
use_cases.description: Prepare a Convex component for reuse across applications with package exports and example validation.

use_cases.title: Integrate Services Safely
use_cases.description: Design integrations that keep secrets and authentication in the app while component logic stays reusable.

prompt_templates.title: Create Local Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a local Convex component for [feature]. First confirm a component is justified, then plan owned tables, functions, wrappers, and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Existing Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my existing Convex feature and extract the reusable backend logic into a component with clear app-facing wrappers.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Design this Convex component as a reusable package. Include package exports, build order, example app checks, and test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Design Hybrid Boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether this feature needs a hybrid Convex component. Compare local, packaged, and hybrid options before coding.

output_examples.input: I need notifications as a local Convex component.
output: A short justification for using a component.
A plan for owned notification tables and public functions.
An app wrapper plan for authentication and client access.

output_examples.input: Package a reusable work queue component for several apps.
output: A package structure with install and typing entry points.
A build and codegen order that avoids stale generated files.
Example app validation steps for type and runtime checks.

output_examples.input: Review my component boundary before implementation.
output: A boundary review for tables, IDs, authentication, secrets, and HTTP routes.
Specific changes to keep app-owned concerns outside the component.

best_practices: Confirm a component is justified before creating new folders.
Keep authentication, secrets, and client wrappers in the app layer.
Run Convex codegen before judging generated imports or component references.
anti_patterns: Putting one-off app logic into a component only to add structure.
Letting component functions access app auth, app table IDs, or environment variables directly.
Publishing a package before an example app validates installation and types.

faq.question: Does this skill write a complete component?
faq.answer: It can guide file structure, schema, functions, wrappers, and validation. Final behavior still depends on project requirements.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it for one-off app logic, thin utilities, or features that do not need isolated Convex state.

faq.question: Does it support packaged components?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for package layout, exports, codegen order, and example app validation.

faq.question: How are secrets handled?
faq.answer: The app layer should read secrets and pass only needed values to trusted server-side component code.

faq.question: Can clients call component functions directly?
faq.answer: No. The skill guides app-side wrappers for client-facing queries, mutations, actions, and HTTP routes.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
